test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which part of a flower develops into a seed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ovule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **ovule** is the part of the flower that develops into a seed after fertilization.
 
• It is located within the ovary of the pistil, which is the female reproductive part of the flower.
 
• After fertilization, the ovule matures into a seed, while the ovary develops into a fruit.
 
• The seed contains the plant embryo along with stored food, which is essential for germination and growth.
 
• Each ovule consists of protective layers (integuments) and a central tissue called the nucellus, where the embryo sac is formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parts of a Flower:**

 
 
• The flower is composed of four main parts: sepals, petals, stamens (male reproductive organs), and pistils (female reproductive organs).
 
• The pistil consists of three main parts: stigma, style, and ovary, where the ovules are housed.
 
 
 
• **Pollination and Fertilization:**
 
 
• Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther (male part) to the stigma (female part).
 
• Fertilization occurs when the male gamete in the pollen fuses with the female gamete in the ovule, forming a zygote.
 
 
 
• **Seed Development:**
 
 
• After fertilization, the zygote develops into an embryo, and the ovule transforms into a seed.
 
• The seed coat develops from the integuments of the ovule, providing protection to the embryo.
 
 
 
• **Fruit Formation:**
 
 
• While the ovule becomes the seed, the ovary of the flower develops into a fruit that protects the seeds and aids in their dispersal.
